newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ex-Suzutan chief indicted for insider trading-Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Suzutan chief indicted for insider trading-Jiji.

text.p: A former president of Suzutan Co Ltd, Katsurao Suzui, was indicted by prosecutors on Thursday for alleged insider trading, Jiji news agency said.
Jiji said prosecutors had also brought similar indictments against four senior executives of the leading retailer of women's wear and a company which managed its assets.
Prosecutors declined to comment and Suzutan spokesmen were not immediately available.

Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission, last month filed a complaint with prosecutors saying that Suzui and some Suzutan officials had sold Suzutan shares before disclosing that it was likely to suffer appraisal losses on its holding of its unit's shares and that there was a possibility the unit would not be able to repay debts guaranteed by Suzutan.

Suzui resigned from the post of president at Suzutan in March. He earlier acknowledged that he had sold 1.01 million Suzutan shares prior to the announcement of a loss for the year to February 28, 1995, but said he did not regard this as improper.
